from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Determinant represents area of a parallelogram.", 
                         "Vectors spanning space define an area.", 
                         "Non-zero determinant means vectors are independent."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: Determinants as Area", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create vectors
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 3], y_range=[-1, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(axes, 'D3')

        v2 = Vector([0, 2], color=RED)
        
        # Parallelogram
        parallelogram = Polygon([0,0,0], [2,0,0], [2,2,0], [0,2,0], color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.3)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(v1), Create(v2))
        self.play(Create(parallelogram))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        label_area = Text("Area = 4", color=GOLD, font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(label_area, 'B4')
        self.play(Write(label_area))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(PURPLE))
        det_label = MathTex(r"det(A) \neq 0", color=PURPLE)
        self.place_at_grid(det_label, 'C5')
        self.play(Write(det_label))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the System Ax = b", [
            "Linear system Ax = b combines vectors.",
            "x and y are scalar weights.",
            "Scaling vectors reaches target point b."
        ])
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 5], y_range=[-1, 5], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(axes, "D3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        a1 = Vector([2, 1], color=YELLOW)
        a2 = Vector([1, 2], color=BLUE)
        b = Vector([3, 3], color=RED)
        
        # Initialize
        self.add(axes)
        self.play(Create(a1), Create(a2))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(b))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        x_weight = 1.0
        y_weight = 1.0
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED)
        
        a1_scaled = Vector([2*x_weight, 1*x_weight], color=YELLOW)
        a2_scaled = Vector([1*y_weight, 2*y_weight], color=BLUE)
        a2_shifted = Vector([1*y_weight, 2*y_weight], color=BLUE).shift(a1_scaled.get_end())
        
        self.play(
            a1.animate.become(a1_scaled),
            a2.animate.become(a2_shifted)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["To solve for x, substitute column.", "This new parallelogram represents the numerator.", "Its area scales with x."]
        self.setup_layout("The Geometry of the Numerator", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define base vectors for the parallelogram
        a1 = np.array([1, 2, 0])
        a2 = np.array([2, 1, 0])
        b = np.array([1.5, 2.5, 0])
        
        # Setup axes
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 4], y_range=[-1, 4], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        self.place_at_grid(axes, "C3", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Parallelogram Mobjects
        orig_para = Polygon(ORIGIN, a1, a1+a2, a2, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        new_para = Polygon(ORIGIN, b, b+a2, a2, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.3)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.add(orig_para)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(orig_para.copy(), new_para))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Indicate scaling
        label = MathTex(r"Area \propto x").next_to(new_para, UP)
        self.add(label)
        self.play(new_para.animate.scale(1.2, about_point=ORIGIN))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Cramer's Rule is a ratio of areas.",
            "x equals the area ratio.",
            "Geometric scaling determines the solution."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis: The Ratio Formula", lecture_lines)
        
        # Formula: x_1 = det(A_1) / det(A)
        formula = MathTex(
            r"x_1 = \frac{\det(A_1)}{\det(A)}",
            font_size=40
        )
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "C3")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(formula))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700") # Gold

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Represent area ratio
        area_a = Square(side_length=2, color=BLUE).set_opacity(0.3)
        area_a1 = Rectangle(width=2, height=4, color=RED).set_opacity(0.3)
        
        self.place_at_grid(area_a, "E2", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(area_a1, "E5", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(area_a), FadeIn(area_a1))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF") # Cyan

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(formula.animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00") # Lime
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Determinants as Area
sections.content: Define the determinant of a 2x2 matrix as the signed area of the parallelogram formed by its column vectors. Establish that a non-zero determinant implies the vectors are linearly independent, spanning a 2D space.
sections.example: A parallelogram defined by vectors v1=(2,0) and v2=(0,2) has a determinant of 4, representing its area.

sections.title: Visualizing the System Ax = b
sections.content: Represent the system of linear equations as a vector combination: x(a1) + y(a2) = b. Geometrically, this means finding the scalar weights (x, y) that scale the column vectors a1 and a2 so that their diagonal sum lands exactly on the target vector b.
sections.example: Imagine a robot arm with two segments. We adjust lengths x and y to reach a target point b in a 2D plane.

sections.title: The Geometry of the Numerator
sections.content: Explain Cramer's substitution. To solve for x, we replace column a1 with vector b. Geometrically, the determinant of this new matrix [b, a2] is the area of the parallelogram formed by b and a2. This area is equivalent to x times the area of the original [a1, a2] parallelogram due to the properties of linear transformations.
sections.example: Show an animation where the parallelogram formed by [a1, a2] is 'stretched' and 'sheared' into the shape formed by [b, a2] as x changes.

sections.title: Synthesis: The Ratio Formula
sections.content: Conclude that x = Det(Ax) / Det(A). This is simply the ratio of the areas. If the area of the new shape is double the original, x must be 2. This intuition bridges the gap between algebraic manipulation and geometric scaling.
sections.example: A scenario where a bird flying at vector b must decide its path relative to two wind vectors, with the 'area ratio' determining the required force.
